title: The Algarve's best par-3 golf courses
excerpt: Two courses where every hole is a par 3, plus one clifftop course with a famous exception — the Algarve's short-game and beginner-friendly rounds, with real par, length and price for each.
hero_image_alt: A golfer putting on the green at Balaia, a par-3 golf course near Albufeira

content.text: Not every round in the Algarve needs to be five hours and eighteen full-length holes. A par-3 course is the fastest way to sharpen your short game, introduce a beginner to golf without intimidating them, or fit in a round on a travel day. This guide compares two genuine all-par-3 courses and a clifftop nine that is home to the region's most famous par 3. They aren't the only short options: Amendoeira, for example, has a nine-hole par-3 Academy course, covered in our guide to [night golf in the Algarve](/guide/night-golf-in-the-algarve).
Vale de Milho — the purest short-game test

Every one of Vale de Milho's nine holes is a par 3, ranging from around 60 to 160 metres, on a hillside above Carvoeiro with sea views from several tees. Dave Thomas — Ryder Cup player and designer of more than 40 courses, including the Belfry — laid it out in 1990, and it's held up as one of the best dedicated short-game venues in the Algarve, not just a beginner's course. A second nine-hole loop with different tee positions is available if you want to play on.
Balaia: short holes in a resort setting

Balaia's nine holes are also all par 3, running from 58 to 160 metres through the grounds of the Balaia Golf Village resort near Albufeira. The short holes make it a relaxed first stop for newer golfers and juniors, and there is a practice range next to the clubhouse if you want to warm up before you play. Note that the resort's guest information says a handicap is required, without giving a limit, so check with the club if you have only just started. On the club's 2025-26 price list, a visitor's day green fee is **€50**.
The [Balaia Golf Village Resort](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/balaia-golf-village.html) sits right on the course, so it's easy to fit in a few holes before breakfast.
Pine Cliffs: four par 3s and one that will test you

Pine Cliffs isn't a pure par-3 course, as four of its nine holes are par 3s and the rest are short par 4s, but it earns its place here for the **Devil's Parlour**, the par-3 sixth, which the club describes as a 197-metre carry over a ravine, to a green perched on the cliff edge. Martin Hawtree designed the course for what's now the Pine Cliffs Resort, and the club's local rules let players without a handicap play from the red tees, so it is genuinely open to newer golfers, even with that one dramatic exception.
Staying at the [Pine Cliffs Residence](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pine-cliffs-residence.html) puts the course, and that cliff-edge tee shot, right outside your door.
Looking for more nine-hole options beyond pure par-3 golf? See our full guide to the [Algarve's 9-hole courses](/algarve-9-hole-courses), which also covers Penina Resort.
